# I.MERGE SOIL GEOPACKAGE WITH SUGARCANE CSV DATA (To run after INLA)

This initial step combines two fundamental datasets that form the foundation of our analysis. The soil geopackage contains spatial information and predictions for various soil properties across different parcels and years, while the sugarcane CSV holds agronomic data including yield measurements, crop management practices, and quality metrics. By merging these datasets on parcel identifiers and campaign years, we create a comprehensive database that links soil characteristics with agricultural outcomes. The script handles potential data quality issues such as duplicate records and inconsistent date formats, ensuring a clean merge that preserves all soil records while adding sugarcane information where available. The output is a unified geopackage that maintains spatial geometry while incorporating both soil and sugarcane variables, with all sugarcane columns clearly prefixed for easy identification.

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# MERGE SOIL GEOPACKAGE WITH SUGARCANE CSV DATA
# Creates combined dataset with all soil predictions + sugarcane variables    
# ============================================================================

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)

cat("========================================\n")
cat("  MERGE SOIL & SUGARCANE DATASETS      \n")
cat("========================================\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: LOAD SOIL GEOPACKAGE DATASET
# ============================================================================
cat("📂 LOADING SOIL GEOPACKAGE DATASET:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

gpkg_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_ALL_VARIABLES_enhanced_predictions2.gpkg"

if (!file.exists(gpkg_path)) {
  stop("❌ Geopackage file not found at: ", gpkg_path)
}

soil_data <- st_read(gpkg_path, quiet = TRUE)
cat("✅ Geopackage loaded successfully\n")
cat("• Total observations:", nrow(soil_data), "\n")
cat("• Total columns:", ncol(soil_data), "\n")
cat("• Unique parcels (field):", length(unique(soil_data$field)), "\n")
cat("• Year range:", min(soil_data$Year, na.rm = TRUE), "-", max(soil_data$Year, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# Store original column order
original_columns <- colnames(soil_data)
cat("• Original soil columns:", length(original_columns), "\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: LOAD SUGARCANE CSV DATASET
# ============================================================================
cat("\n📂 LOADING SUGARCANE CSV DATASET:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

csv_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/sugarcane_data_converted.csv"

if (!file.exists(csv_path)) {
  stop("❌ CSV file not found at: ", csv_path)
}

sugarcane_data <- read_csv(csv_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
cat("✅ CSV loaded successfully\n")
cat("• Total observations:", nrow(sugarcane_data), "\n")
cat("• Total columns:", ncol(sugarcane_data), "\n")

# Identify parcel and campaign columns (case-insensitive)
parcel_col <- grep("^parcel$|^parcelle$|^field$", 
                   colnames(sugarcane_data), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
campaign_col <- grep("^campaign$|^campagne$", 
                     colnames(sugarcane_data), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)

if (length(parcel_col) == 0 || length(campaign_col) == 0) {
  stop("❌ Could not find parcel or campaign columns in CSV")
}

cat("• Parcel column identified:", parcel_col[1], "\n")
cat("• Campaign column identified:", campaign_col[1], "\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: PREPARE SUGARCANE DATA
# ============================================================================
cat("\n🔄 PREPARING SUGARCANE DATA:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

# Convert campaign to year
convert_campaign_to_year <- function(campaign) {
  if (is.na(campaign)) return(NA_integer_)
  
  # Extract first part (e.g., "03" from "03-04")
  first_part <- sub("-.*", "", as.character(campaign))
  first_part <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", first_part)
  
  if (nchar(first_part) == 0) return(NA_integer_)
  
  year_short <- as.integer(first_part)
  
  # Convert 2-digit year to 4-digit
  if (year_short <= 50) {
    year_full <- 2000 + year_short
  } else {
    year_full <- 1900 + year_short
  }
  
  return(year_full)
}

# Rename and prepare sugarcane data
sugarcane_prepared <- sugarcane_data %>%
  rename(
    field = !!parcel_col[1],
    Campaign = !!campaign_col[1]
  ) %>%
  mutate(Year = sapply(Campaign, convert_campaign_to_year)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Year)) %>%
  # Remove any columns that might conflict with soil data
  select(-any_of(c("geometry", "geom")))

cat("✅ Sugarcane data prepared\n")
cat("• Observations with valid year:", nrow(sugarcane_prepared), "\n")
cat("• Unique field-year combinations:", 
    nrow(distinct(sugarcane_prepared, field, Year)), "\n")

# Show sugarcane columns (excluding field, Year, Campaign)
sugarcane_columns <- setdiff(colnames(sugarcane_prepared), c("field", "Year", "Campaign"))
cat("• Sugarcane variables to add:", length(sugarcane_columns), "\n")

if (length(sugarcane_columns) > 0) {
  cat("\n📋 Sugarcane variables:\n")
  for (i in seq_along(sugarcane_columns)) {
    col_name <- sugarcane_columns[i]
    non_na <- sum(!is.na(sugarcane_prepared[[col_name]]))
    cat(sprintf("  %2d. %-30s (%d non-NA values)\n", i, col_name, non_na))
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: CHECK FOR DUPLICATE FIELD-YEAR COMBINATIONS IN SUGARCANE DATA
# ============================================================================
cat("\n🔍 CHECKING FOR DUPLICATES IN SUGARCANE DATA:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

# Check for duplicates
duplicate_check <- sugarcane_prepared %>%
  group_by(field, Year) %>%
  summarise(n_records = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_records > 1)

if (nrow(duplicate_check) > 0) {
  cat("⚠️  Found", nrow(duplicate_check), "field-year combinations with multiple records\n")
  cat("• Total duplicate records:", sum(duplicate_check$n_records), "\n")
  
  # Show some examples
  cat("\nExamples of duplicates:\n")
  print(head(duplicate_check, 10))
  
  cat("\n🔧 HANDLING DUPLICATES:\n")
  cat("Strategy: Aggregating numeric columns (mean) and keeping first value for non-numeric\n")
  
  # Aggregate duplicates
  sugarcane_aggregated <- sugarcane_prepared %>%
    group_by(field, Year, Campaign) %>%
    summarise(
      across(where(is.numeric), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      across(where(~!is.numeric(.x)), ~first(na.omit(.x))),
      n_original_records = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  cat("✅ Duplicates aggregated\n")
  cat("• Original records:", nrow(sugarcane_prepared), "\n")
  cat("• After aggregation:", nrow(sugarcane_aggregated), "\n")
  
  sugarcane_prepared <- sugarcane_aggregated
  
} else {
  cat("✅ No duplicate field-year combinations found\n")
  
  # Add n_original_records column for consistency
  sugarcane_prepared <- sugarcane_prepared %>%
    mutate(n_original_records = 1)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: MERGE DATASETS
# ============================================================================
cat("\n🔗 MERGING DATASETS:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

cat("Merge strategy: LEFT JOIN (keep all soil records, add sugarcane data where available)\n")

# Create merge key
soil_data <- soil_data %>%
  mutate(merge_key = paste(field, Year, sep = "_"))

sugarcane_prepared <- sugarcane_prepared %>%
  mutate(merge_key = paste(field, Year, sep = "_"))

cat("• Soil records:", nrow(soil_data), "\n")
cat("• Sugarcane records:", nrow(sugarcane_prepared), "\n")
cat("• Unique soil merge keys:", length(unique(soil_data$merge_key)), "\n")
cat("• Unique sugarcane merge keys:", length(unique(sugarcane_prepared$merge_key)), "\n")

# Find matching keys
matching_keys <- intersect(soil_data$merge_key, sugarcane_prepared$merge_key)
cat("• Matching merge keys:", length(matching_keys), "\n")
cat("• Match rate:", round(length(matching_keys) / length(unique(soil_data$merge_key)) * 100, 2), "%\n")

# Prepare sugarcane data for merge (remove duplicate key columns)
sugarcane_for_merge <- sugarcane_prepared %>%
  select(-field, -Year) %>%  # These are already in soil_data
  # Prefix sugarcane columns to avoid conflicts
  rename_with(~paste0("SC_", .), .cols = -merge_key)

cat("\n🔄 Performing left join...\n")

# Perform the merge
merged_data <- soil_data %>%
  left_join(sugarcane_for_merge, by = "merge_key", relationship = "many-to-one")

# Remove temporary merge_key
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  select(-merge_key)

cat("✅ Merge completed\n")
cat("• Final dataset rows:", nrow(merged_data), "\n")
cat("• Final dataset columns:", ncol(merged_data), "\n")

# Check how many rows got sugarcane data
rows_with_sugarcane <- sum(!is.na(merged_data$SC_Campaign))
cat("• Rows with sugarcane data:", rows_with_sugarcane, 
    "(", round(rows_with_sugarcane/nrow(merged_data)*100, 2), "%)\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: REORDER COLUMNS (SUGARCANE AT END)
# ============================================================================
cat("\n📋 REORDERING COLUMNS:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

# Get soil columns (original) and sugarcane columns (new)
soil_cols <- intersect(original_columns, colnames(merged_data))
sugarcane_cols <- colnames(merged_data)[grepl("^SC_", colnames(merged_data))]
geometry_col <- "geom"

# Reorder: soil columns first, then sugarcane columns, geometry last
if (geometry_col %in% colnames(merged_data)) {
  soil_cols <- setdiff(soil_cols, geometry_col)
  merged_data <- merged_data %>%
    select(all_of(soil_cols), all_of(sugarcane_cols), all_of(geometry_col))
} else {
  merged_data <- merged_data %>%
    select(all_of(soil_cols), all_of(sugarcane_cols))
}

cat("✅ Columns reordered\n")
cat("• Soil columns:", length(soil_cols), "\n")
cat("• Sugarcane columns:", length(sugarcane_cols), "\n")
cat("• Total columns:", ncol(merged_data), "\n")

# Show column structure
cat("\n📊 FINAL COLUMN STRUCTURE:\n")
cat("First 10 soil columns:\n")
print(head(soil_cols, 10))

cat("\nSugarcane columns (all prefixed with 'SC_'):\n")
print(sugarcane_cols)

# ============================================================================
# STEP 7: GENERATE SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================
cat("\n📊 GENERATING SUMMARY STATISTICS:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

# Create summary by year
summary_by_year <- merged_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Records = n(),
    With_Sugarcane_Data = sum(!is.na(SC_Campaign)),
    Pct_With_Sugarcane = round(sum(!is.na(SC_Campaign)) / n() * 100, 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year)

cat("Summary by year:\n")
print(summary_by_year)

# Overall statistics
cat("\n📈 OVERALL STATISTICS:\n")
cat("• Total merged records:", nrow(merged_data), "\n")
cat("• Records with sugarcane data:", sum(!is.na(merged_data$SC_Campaign)), "\n")
cat("• Records without sugarcane data:", sum(is.na(merged_data$SC_Campaign)), "\n")
cat("• Overall match rate:", 
    round(sum(!is.na(merged_data$SC_Campaign))/nrow(merged_data)*100, 2), "%\n")

# Check for any completely empty sugarcane columns
empty_sugarcane_cols <- sugarcane_cols[sapply(merged_data[sugarcane_cols], function(x) all(is.na(x)))]
if (length(empty_sugarcane_cols) > 0) {
  cat("\n⚠️  Empty sugarcane columns (all NA):\n")
  print(empty_sugarcane_cols)
} else {
  cat("\n✅ All sugarcane columns have at least some data\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 8: SAVE MERGED GEOPACKAGE
# ============================================================================
cat("\n💾 SAVING MERGED GEOPACKAGE:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 40), "\n", sep="")

output_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane.gpkg"

cat("Writing to:", output_path, "\n")
st_write(merged_data, output_path, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
cat("✅ Merged geopackage saved successfully\n")

# Also save as CSV (attributes only)
csv_output_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane_attributes.csv"
st_drop_geometry(merged_data) %>% write_csv(csv_output_path)
cat("✅ CSV attributes saved:", basename(csv_output_path), "\n")

# Save summary statistics
summary_output_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/MERGE_summary_by_year.csv"
write_csv(summary_by_year, summary_output_path)
cat("✅ Summary statistics saved:", basename(summary_output_path), "\n")
```

# II. CALCULATE GROWING SEASON RAINFALL WITH PRO-RATA FOR PARTIAL MONTHS (To run after Rainfall Data Preprocessing)

Rainfall during the growing season is a critical determinant of crop yield, but calculating it accurately requires more than simple summation. This section addresses the complexity of aggregating monthly rainfall data when planting and harvest dates don't align perfectly with calendar months. The script implements a pro-rata calculation method that proportionally accounts for partial months at the start and end of each growing period. For example, if a crop is planted on October 15th, only the rainfall from the 15th through the 31st of October is counted, appropriately weighted by the number of days. This approach ensures that rainfall totals accurately reflect the water available during each specific growing period, rather than artificially inflating or deflating values by including irrelevant time periods. The output adds several new variables to the dataset including total growing season rainfall, the number of days in the growing season, and average daily rainfall.

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# ============================================================================
# This script calculates total rainfall during the growing season for each
# parcel, using pro-rata calculation for partial months at start/end dates
# ============================================================================

library(sf)
library(terra)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================================

gpkg_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane.gpkg"
monthly_results_dir <- "batch_matern_kriging_results_extended"
output_gpkg <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane_with_growing_season_rainfall.gpkg"

cat("============================================\n")
cat("  GROWING SEASON RAINFALL CALCULATOR       \n")
cat("============================================\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: LOAD PARCELS
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 1: Loading parcels...\n")

parcels <- st_read(gpkg_path, quiet = TRUE)

cat("  Loaded", nrow(parcels), "records\n")

# Check required columns
required_cols <- c("field", "SC_planting_date", "SC_harvest_date")
missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(parcels))

if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop("Missing required columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
}

cat("  Required columns found\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: PARSE AND VALIDATE DATES
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 2: Parsing dates...\n")

# First, check what format the dates are in
cat("  Checking date format...\n")
sample_planting <- head(parcels$SC_planting_date, 3)
sample_harvest <- head(parcels$SC_harvest_date, 3)
cat("  Sample planting dates:", paste(sample_planting, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("  Sample harvest dates:", paste(sample_harvest, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Try multiple date parsing strategies
parse_flexible_date <- function(date_string) {
  # If already a Date object, return as is
  if (inherits(date_string, "Date")) {
    return(date_string)
  }
  
  # Convert to character if factor
  date_string <- as.character(date_string)
  
  # Try different formats
  result <- suppressWarnings(dmy(date_string))  # DD/MM/YYYY
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(mdy(date_string))  # MM/DD/YYYY
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(ymd(date_string))  # YYYY-MM-DD
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%d/%m/%Y"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%Y-%m-%d"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  # If all fail, return NA
  return(as.Date(NA))
}

# Parse dates with flexible function
parcels <- parcels %>%
  mutate(
    planting_date = sapply(SC_planting_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01"),
    harvest_date = sapply(SC_harvest_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01")
  )

# Check for parsing issues
n_valid <- sum(!is.na(parcels$planting_date) & !is.na(parcels$harvest_date))
n_invalid <- nrow(parcels) - n_valid

cat("  Valid date pairs:", n_valid, "\n")
cat("  Invalid date pairs:", n_invalid, "\n")

if (n_invalid > 0) {
  cat("  Warning: Some records have invalid dates and will be skipped\n")
  cat("  Example invalid dates:\n")
  invalid_examples <- parcels %>%
    filter(is.na(planting_date) | is.na(harvest_date)) %>%
    select(field, SC_planting_date, SC_harvest_date) %>%
    head(3)
  print(invalid_examples)
}

# Filter to valid dates only
parcels_valid <- parcels %>%
  filter(!is.na(planting_date), !is.na(harvest_date), harvest_date > planting_date)

cat("  Working with", nrow(parcels_valid), "valid records\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: LOAD MONTHLY RASTERS AND CREATE INDEX
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 3: Loading monthly rainfall rasters...\n")

# Find all monthly folders
monthly_folders <- list.dirs(monthly_results_dir, recursive = FALSE)
monthly_folders <- monthly_folders[grepl("month_\\d{4}_\\d{2}", basename(monthly_folders))]

# Function to load var1.pred band only
load_monthly_raster <- function(folder_path) {
  utm_path <- file.path(folder_path, "kriging_extended_utm28n.tif")
  wgs_path <- file.path(folder_path, "kriging_extended_wgs84.tif")
  
  raster_path <- NULL
  if (file.exists(utm_path)) {
    raster_path <- utm_path
  } else if (file.exists(wgs_path)) {
    raster_path <- wgs_path
  }
  
  if (is.null(raster_path)) return(NULL)
  
  r <- rast(raster_path)
  
  if (nlyr(r) > 1) {
    band_names <- names(r)
    pred_band_idx <- which(band_names == "var1.pred")
    if (length(pred_band_idx) > 0) {
      r <- r[[pred_band_idx]]
    } else {
      r <- r[[1]]
    }
  }
  
  return(r)
}

# Create raster index
raster_index <- data.frame(
  folder = monthly_folders,
  basename = basename(monthly_folders),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    year_month = gsub("month_", "", basename),
    year = as.integer(substr(year_month, 1, 4)),
    month = as.integer(substr(year_month, 6, 7)),
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, "01", sep = "-"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(date)

cat("  Found", nrow(raster_index), "monthly rasters\n")
min_date_str <- format(min(raster_index$date), "%Y-%m")
max_date_str <- format(max(raster_index$date), "%Y-%m")
cat("  Date range:", min_date_str, "to", max_date_str, "\n\n")

# Load all rasters into a list
monthly_rasters <- list()
cat("  Loading rasters into memory...\n")

for (i in 1:nrow(raster_index)) {
  r <- load_monthly_raster(raster_index$folder[i])
  if (!is.null(r)) {
    key <- format(raster_index$date[i], "%Y-%m")
    monthly_rasters[[key]] <- r
    if (i %% 50 == 0) cat("    Loaded", i, "/", nrow(raster_index), "\n")
  }
}

cat("  Successfully loaded", length(monthly_rasters), "rasters\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: CALCULATE GROWING SEASON RAINFALL FOR EACH PARCEL
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 4: Calculating growing season rainfall...\n")

# Ensure parcels are in same CRS as rasters
first_raster <- monthly_rasters[[1]]
parcels_projected <- st_transform(parcels_valid, crs(first_raster))

# Function to calculate pro-rata rainfall for a date range
calculate_growing_season_rainfall <- function(parcel_geom, planting_date, harvest_date, 
                                              raster_index, monthly_rasters) {
  
  # Get all months in the growing season
  start_year_month <- floor_date(planting_date, "month")
  end_year_month <- floor_date(harvest_date, "month")
  
  # Generate sequence of months
  month_seq <- seq(start_year_month, end_year_month, by = "month")
  
  total_rainfall <- 0
  months_processed <- 0
  
  for (i in seq_along(month_seq)) {
    month_date <- as.Date(month_seq[i], origin = "1970-01-01")
    month_key <- format(month_date, "%Y-%m")
    
    # Check if we have data for this month
    if (!month_key %in% names(monthly_rasters)) {
      next
    }
    
    # Get the raster
    month_raster <- monthly_rasters[[month_key]]
    
    # Extract rainfall value for this parcel
    rainfall_value <- terra::extract(
      month_raster,
      vect(parcel_geom),
      fun = mean,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )[1, 2]
    
    if (is.na(rainfall_value)) {
      next
    }
    
    # Calculate days in this month
    days_in_month <- days_in_month(month_date)
    
    # Calculate pro-rata factor
    if (month_date == start_year_month && month_date == end_year_month) {
      # Both planting and harvest in same month
      days_used <- as.numeric(harvest_date - planting_date) + 1
      pro_rata_factor <- days_used / days_in_month
      
    } else if (month_date == start_year_month) {
      # First month (partial)
      days_used <- days_in_month - day(planting_date) + 1
      pro_rata_factor <- days_used / days_in_month
      
    } else if (month_date == end_year_month) {
      # Last month (partial)
      days_used <- day(harvest_date)
      pro_rata_factor <- days_used / days_in_month
      
    } else {
      # Full month
      pro_rata_factor <- 1.0
    }
    
    # Add pro-rated rainfall
    total_rainfall <- total_rainfall + (rainfall_value * pro_rata_factor)
    months_processed <- months_processed + 1
  }
  
  return(list(
    total_rainfall = total_rainfall,
    months_processed = months_processed,
    growing_days = as.numeric(harvest_date - planting_date) + 1
  ))
}

# Process each parcel
results_list <- list()

cat("  Processing parcels...\n")

for (i in 1:nrow(parcels_projected)) {
  
  if (i %% 100 == 0) {
    cat("    Progress:", i, "/", nrow(parcels_projected), "\n")
  }
  
  result <- calculate_growing_season_rainfall(
    parcel_geom = parcels_projected[i, ],
    planting_date = parcels_projected$planting_date[i],
    harvest_date = parcels_projected$harvest_date[i],
    raster_index = raster_index,
    monthly_rasters = monthly_rasters
  )
  
  results_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    row_id = i,
    field = parcels_projected$field[i],
    growing_season_rainfall_mm = result$total_rainfall,
    growing_season_days = result$growing_days,
    months_with_data = result$months_processed,
    avg_daily_rainfall_mm = result$total_rainfall / result$growing_days
  )
}

# Combine results
results_df <- bind_rows(results_list)

cat("  Completed!\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: MERGE RESULTS BACK TO ORIGINAL PARCELS
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 5: Merging results to parcels...\n")

# Add a unique identifier to match exact rows
parcels_valid$row_num <- 1:nrow(parcels_valid)
results_df$row_num <- results_df$row_id

# Create results with row matching info
results_for_merge <- results_df %>%
  select(row_num, growing_season_rainfall_mm, growing_season_days, 
         months_with_data, avg_daily_rainfall_mm)

# Add row numbers to original parcels based on valid dates
parcels <- parcels %>%
  mutate(
    planting_date_temp = sapply(SC_planting_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% 
      as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01"),
    harvest_date_temp = sapply(SC_harvest_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% 
      as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01"),
    is_valid = !is.na(planting_date_temp) & !is.na(harvest_date_temp) & 
               harvest_date_temp > planting_date_temp
  )

# Assign row numbers only to valid parcels
valid_indices <- which(parcels$is_valid)
parcels$row_num <- NA_integer_
parcels$row_num[valid_indices] <- 1:length(valid_indices)

# Merge results only for valid parcels
parcels_final <- parcels %>%
  left_join(
    results_for_merge,
    by = "row_num"
  ) %>%
  select(-planting_date_temp, -harvest_date_temp, -is_valid, -row_num)

# Count results
n_with_rainfall <- sum(!is.na(parcels_final$growing_season_rainfall_mm))
n_without_rainfall <- sum(is.na(parcels_final$growing_season_rainfall_mm))

cat("  Merged successfully\n")
cat("  Records with rainfall data:", n_with_rainfall, "\n")
cat("  Records without rainfall data (invalid dates):", n_without_rainfall, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: SAVE NEW GEOPACKAGE
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 6: Saving new geopackage...\n")

st_write(parcels_final, output_gpkg, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

cat("  Saved to:", output_gpkg, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

cat("============================================\n")
cat("  SUMMARY STATISTICS                       \n")
cat("============================================\n\n")

summary_stats <- results_df %>%
  filter(growing_season_rainfall_mm > 0) %>%
  summarise(
    n_parcels = n(),
    mean_rainfall = mean(growing_season_rainfall_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rainfall = median(growing_season_rainfall_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rainfall = min(growing_season_rainfall_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rainfall = max(growing_season_rainfall_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_rainfall = sd(growing_season_rainfall_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_days = mean(growing_season_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_daily_rain = mean(avg_daily_rainfall_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat("Parcels processed:", as.character(summary_stats$n_parcels), "\n")
cat("Growing season rainfall (mm):\n")
cat("  Mean:", sprintf("%.1f", summary_stats$mean_rainfall), "\n")
cat("  Median:", sprintf("%.1f", summary_stats$median_rainfall), "\n")
cat("  Range:", sprintf("%.1f", summary_stats$min_rainfall), "-", 
    sprintf("%.1f", summary_stats$max_rainfall), "\n")
cat("  SD:", sprintf("%.1f", summary_stats$sd_rainfall), "\n\n")

cat("Growing season length:\n")
cat("  Mean days:", sprintf("%.1f", summary_stats$mean_days), "\n")
cat("  Mean daily rainfall:", sprintf("%.2f", summary_stats$mean_daily_rain), "mm/day\n\n")

# Show examples
cat("Example parcels:\n")
examples <- results_df %>%
  filter(growing_season_rainfall_mm > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(growing_season_rainfall_mm)) %>%
  head(5)

for (i in 1:nrow(examples)) {
  cat("  Field:", as.character(examples$field[i]), "\n")
  cat("    Total rainfall:", sprintf("%.1f", examples$growing_season_rainfall_mm[i]), "mm\n")
  cat("    Growing days:", as.character(examples$growing_season_days[i]), "\n")
  cat("    Avg daily:", sprintf("%.2f", examples$avg_daily_rainfall_mm[i]), "mm/day\n\n")
}
gc()
```

# III. WEATHER DATA INTEGRATION WITH YIELD-SOIL Data - Geopackage (To run after Weather Data Preprocessing)

Weather conditions during crop development profoundly influence final yield outcomes, often in ways that simple averages cannot capture. This major section integrates comprehensive daily weather data into our geopackage, calculating both standard climate statistics and extreme weather indices over each growing period. The integration is performed in two progressive steps: first calculating basic mean values for temperature, humidity, radiation, and evaporation, then adding sophisticated extreme indices that capture the frequency and intensity of weather events that stress crops. These extreme indices, based on internationally recognized standards from the Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices (ETCCDI), provide crucial information about drought periods, heat waves, heavy rainfall events, and temperature extremes that can dramatically impact sugar accumulation and final tonnage, often explaining yield variations that basic averages miss entirely.

## III.1. Growing Season Weather Aggregation (Basic Means)

This foundational weather integration step calculates straightforward statistical summaries of daily weather variables over each parcel's growing period. For every temperature, humidity, and soil temperature measurement in the daily weather dataset, we compute the mean value experienced from planting to harvest. Additionally, cumulative totals are calculated for precipitation, solar radiation, and evaporation, providing measures of total energy and water inputs during crop development. The script carefully handles date parsing from multiple formats and validates that growing periods fall within the available weather data coverage. These basic statistics serve as essential baseline predictors for yield models while also providing context for interpreting the more sophisticated extreme indices added in the next step.

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# INTEGRATE WEATHER DATA INTO GEOPACKAGE WITH GROWING SEASON CALCULATIONS
# ============================================================================
# This script adds weather variables calculated over growing periods
# to the geopackage with rainfall data
# ============================================================================

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(readr)

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================================

# Input geopackage (output from rainfall calculation)
input_gpkg <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane_with_growing_season_rainfall.gpkg"

# Weather data file
weather_file_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/BD_weather_with_ERA5_radiation.csv"

# Output geopackage
output_gpkg <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane_with_weather.gpkg"

cat("============================================\n")
cat("  WEATHER DATA INTEGRATION                 \n")
cat("============================================\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: LOAD GEOPACKAGE
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 1: Loading geopackage...\n")

if (!file.exists(input_gpkg)) {
  stop("Error: Geopackage not found at: ", input_gpkg)
}

parcels <- st_read(input_gpkg, quiet = TRUE)

cat("  Loaded", nrow(parcels), "parcels\n")
cat("  Columns:", ncol(parcels), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: LOAD WEATHER DATA
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 2: Loading weather data...\n")

if (!file.exists(weather_file_path)) {
  stop("Error: Weather data file not found at: ", weather_file_path)
}

# Import weather data with multiple encoding attempts
weather_data <- NULL

tryCatch({
  weather_data <- read_csv2(weather_file_path, 
                           locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8", decimal_mark = ","), 
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
  cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (UTF-8)\n")
}, error = function(e) {
  tryCatch({
    weather_data <<- read_csv2(weather_file_path, 
                              locale = locale(encoding = "latin1", decimal_mark = ","), 
                              show_col_types = FALSE)
    cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (latin1)\n")
  }, error = function(e2) {
    tryCatch({
      weather_data <<- read_csv2(weather_file_path, 
                                locale = locale(encoding = "CP1252", decimal_mark = ","), 
                                show_col_types = FALSE)
      cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (CP1252)\n")
    }, error = function(e3) {
      weather_data <<- read.csv(weather_file_path, sep = ";", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, 
                               encoding = "UTF-8", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
      cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (base R)\n")
    })
  })
})

# Clean column names
if (!is.null(weather_data)) {
  original_names <- names(weather_data)
  clean_names <- iconv(original_names, from = "UTF-8", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
  clean_names <- gsub("T�\\(C\\)", "T_C", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("Cl�", "Cle", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("P�riode", "Periode", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("D�cade", "Decade", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("Ann�e", "Annee", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("S�n�gal", "Senegal", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("�", "e", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("�", "a", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._]", "_", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("__+", "_", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("^_|_$", "", clean_names)
  names(weather_data) <- clean_names
  cat("  ✓ Column names cleaned\n")
}

cat("  Weather data:", nrow(weather_data), "records\n")
cat("  Date range:", as.character(range(weather_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: PARSE DATES IN PARCELS
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 3: Parsing dates in parcels...\n")

# Function to parse dates flexibly
parse_flexible_date <- function(date_string) {
  if (inherits(date_string, "Date")) return(date_string)
  date_string <- as.character(date_string)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(dmy(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(mdy(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(ymd(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%d/%m/%Y"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%Y-%m-%d"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  return(as.Date(NA))
}

# Parse planting and harvest dates
parcels <- parcels %>%
  mutate(
    planting_date = sapply(SC_planting_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% 
      as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01"),
    harvest_date = sapply(SC_harvest_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% 
      as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01")
  )

# Check validity
weather_date_range <- range(weather_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE)
valid_records <- !is.na(parcels$planting_date) & 
                 !is.na(parcels$harvest_date) & 
                 parcels$planting_date < parcels$harvest_date &
                 parcels$planting_date >= weather_date_range[1] & 
                 parcels$harvest_date <= weather_date_range[2]

cat("  Valid growing periods:", sum(valid_records), "out of", nrow(parcels), "\n")
cat("  Date range:", as.character(range(parcels$planting_date[valid_records], na.rm = TRUE)), "to",
    as.character(range(parcels$harvest_date[valid_records], na.rm = TRUE)), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: CALCULATE WEATHER STATISTICS FOR EACH PARCEL
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 4: Calculating weather statistics...\n")

# Function to calculate weather statistics for a growing period
calculate_weather_stats <- function(plant_date, harvest_date, weather_df) {
  if (is.na(plant_date) || is.na(harvest_date) || plant_date >= harvest_date) {
    return(list(
      temp_mini_mean = NA, temp_maxi_mean = NA, temp_moy_mean = NA, ampl_mean = NA,
      h_mini_mean = NA, h_maxi_mean = NA, h_moy_mean = NA,
      h_6h_mean = NA, h_12h_mean = NA, h_16h_mean = NA, h_24h_mean = NA,
      t_6h_10cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_10cm_ir_mean = NA,
      t_6h_20cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_20cm_ir_mean = NA,
      t_6h_30cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_30cm_ir_mean = NA,
      t_6h_50cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_50cm_ir_mean = NA,
      precipitation_weather_total = NA, radiation_total = NA, 
      radiation_ERA_total = NA, evaporation_total = NA,
      growing_period_days_weather = NA
    ))
  }
  
  # Filter weather data for the growing period
  period_weather <- weather_df[weather_df$Date >= plant_date & weather_df$Date <= harvest_date, ]
  
  if (nrow(period_weather) == 0) {
    return(list(
      temp_mini_mean = NA, temp_maxi_mean = NA, temp_moy_mean = NA, ampl_mean = NA,
      h_mini_mean = NA, h_maxi_mean = NA, h_moy_mean = NA,
      h_6h_mean = NA, h_12h_mean = NA, h_16h_mean = NA, h_24h_mean = NA,
      t_6h_10cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_10cm_ir_mean = NA,
      t_6h_20cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_20cm_ir_mean = NA,
      t_6h_30cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_30cm_ir_mean = NA,
      t_6h_50cm_ir_mean = NA, t_16h_50cm_ir_mean = NA,
      precipitation_weather_total = NA, radiation_total = NA, 
      radiation_ERA_total = NA, evaporation_total = NA,
      growing_period_days_weather = as.numeric(harvest_date - plant_date)
    ))
  }
  
  # Calculate statistics
  stats <- list(
    # Temperature means
    temp_mini_mean = mean(period_weather$T_C_mini, na.rm = TRUE),
    temp_maxi_mean = mean(period_weather$T_C_maxi, na.rm = TRUE),
    temp_moy_mean = mean(period_weather$T_C_moy, na.rm = TRUE),
    ampl_mean = mean(period_weather$Ampl, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Humidity means
    h_mini_mean = mean(period_weather$H_Mini, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_maxi_mean = mean(period_weather$H_Maxi, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_moy_mean = mean(period_weather$H_Moy, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_6h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_6_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_12h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_12_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_16h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_16_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_24h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_24_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Soil temperature means (irrigated)
    t_6h_10cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_6h_10_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_16h_10cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_16h_10_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_6h_20cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_6h_20_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_16h_20cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_16h_20_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_6h_30cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_6h_30_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_16h_30cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_16h_30_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_6h_50cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_6h_50_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_16h_50cm_ir_mean = mean(period_weather$T_16h_50_cm_Ir, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Accumulations (note: renamed precipitation to avoid conflict)
    precipitation_weather_total = sum(period_weather$precipitation_stations_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    radiation_total = sum(period_weather$Radiation, na.rm = TRUE),
    radiation_ERA_total = sum(period_weather$Radiation_ERA, na.rm = TRUE),
    evaporation_total = sum(period_weather$Ev_C2, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Growing period length
    growing_period_days_weather = as.numeric(harvest_date - plant_date)
  )
  
  # Convert NaN to NA
  stats <- lapply(stats, function(x) if(is.nan(x)) NA else x)
  
  return(stats)
}

# Initialize weather variables dataframe
n_total <- nrow(parcels)
weather_vars <- data.frame(
  temp_mini_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  temp_maxi_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  temp_moy_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  ampl_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_mini_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_maxi_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_moy_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_6h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_12h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_16h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_24h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_6h_10cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_16h_10cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_6h_20cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_16h_20cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_6h_30cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_16h_30cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_6h_50cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  t_16h_50cm_ir_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  precipitation_weather_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  radiation_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  radiation_ERA_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  evaporation_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  growing_period_days_weather = rep(NA_real_, n_total)
)

# Process each parcel
chunk_size <- ceiling(n_total / 10)

for (i in 1:n_total) {
  if (i %% chunk_size == 0 || i == n_total) {
    cat("  Processing:", i, "/", n_total, "(", round(100*i/n_total, 1), "%)\n")
  }
  
  stats <- calculate_weather_stats(
    plant_date = parcels$planting_date[i],
    harvest_date = parcels$harvest_date[i],
    weather_df = weather_data
  )
  
  # Assign results
  for (var_name in names(stats)) {
    weather_vars[i, var_name] <- stats[[var_name]]
  }
}

cat("  Completed!\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: MERGE WEATHER DATA WITH PARCELS
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 5: Merging weather data with parcels...\n")

# Combine parcels with weather variables
parcels_with_weather <- cbind(
  parcels %>% select(-planting_date, -harvest_date),  # Remove temp date columns
  weather_vars
)

# Count successful calculations
n_with_weather <- sum(!is.na(weather_vars$growing_period_days_weather))

cat("  Records with weather data:", n_with_weather, "\n")
cat("  Records without weather data:", n_total - n_with_weather, "\n")
cat("  Total columns in output:", ncol(parcels_with_weather), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: SAVE OUTPUT GEOPACKAGE
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 6: Saving output geopackage...\n")

st_write(parcels_with_weather, output_gpkg, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

cat("  Saved to:", output_gpkg, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

cat("============================================\n")
cat("  SUMMARY STATISTICS                       \n")
cat("============================================\n\n")

valid_weather <- weather_vars %>%
  filter(!is.na(growing_period_days_weather))

if (nrow(valid_weather) > 0) {
  cat("Valid weather calculations:", nrow(valid_weather), "\n\n")
  
  cat("Temperature statistics (°C):\n")
  cat("  Mean minimum:", sprintf("%.2f", mean(valid_weather$temp_mini_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n")
  cat("  Mean maximum:", sprintf("%.2f", mean(valid_weather$temp_maxi_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n")
  cat("  Mean average:", sprintf("%.2f", mean(valid_weather$temp_moy_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n\n")
  
  cat("Humidity statistics (%):\n")
  cat("  Mean minimum:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$h_mini_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n")
  cat("  Mean maximum:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$h_maxi_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n")
  cat("  Mean average:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$h_moy_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n\n")
  
  cat("Accumulation statistics:\n")
  cat("  Mean precipitation:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$precipitation_weather_total, na.rm = TRUE)), "mm\n")
  cat("  Mean radiation:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$radiation_total, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n")
  cat("  Mean ERA5 radiation:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$radiation_ERA_total, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n")
  cat("  Mean evaporation:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$evaporation_total, na.rm = TRUE)), "mm\n\n")
  
  cat("Growing period length:\n")
  cat("  Mean:", sprintf("%.1f", mean(valid_weather$growing_period_days_weather, na.rm = TRUE)), "days\n")
  cat("  Range:", sprintf("%.0f", min(valid_weather$growing_period_days_weather, na.rm = TRUE)), "-",
      sprintf("%.0f", max(valid_weather$growing_period_days_weather, na.rm = TRUE)), "days\n\n")
}
cat("Output file:", output_gpkg, "\n")
```

## III.2. Extreme Weather Indices Integration

While average weather conditions matter, crops often respond more strongly to extreme events that occur during critical growth phases. This advanced section calculates nine extreme rainfall indices and five extreme temperature indices that capture the character and intensity of weather extremes during each growing season. The rainfall indices identify patterns like consecutive dry days that cause drought stress, maximum rainfall over short periods that can cause waterlogging, and the contribution of extreme precipitation events to total water availability. Temperature indices quantify heat stress by counting hot days above critical thresholds and recording the absolute temperature extremes experienced. These indices are particularly valuable for machine learning models because they capture non-linear relationships between weather and yield that mean values cannot represent, often improving prediction accuracy by ten to thirty percent in agricultural applications. The calculations use robust statistical methods including percentile-based thresholds and rolling window maximums to ensure indices are meaningful across different growing seasons and conditions.

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# INTEGRATE WEATHER DATA WITH EXTREME INDICES INTO GEOPACKAGE
# ============================================================================
# This script adds weather variables AND extreme weather indices calculated 
# over growing periods to the geopackage with rainfall data
# ============================================================================

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(readr)
library(zoo)  # For rolling calculations

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================================

# Input geopackage (output from rainfall calculation)
input_gpkg <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane_with_growing_season_rainfall.gpkg"

# Weather data file
weather_file_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/BD_weather_with_ERA5_radiation.csv"

# Output geopackage
output_gpkg <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane_with_weather_extreme_indices.gpkg"

cat("============================================\n")
cat("  WEATHER DATA WITH EXTREME INDICES        \n")
cat("============================================\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: LOAD GEOPACKAGE
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 1: Loading geopackage...\n")

if (!file.exists(input_gpkg)) {
  stop("Error: Geopackage not found at: ", input_gpkg)
}

parcels <- st_read(input_gpkg, quiet = TRUE)

cat("  Loaded", nrow(parcels), "parcels\n")
cat("  Columns:", ncol(parcels), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: LOAD WEATHER DATA
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 2: Loading weather data...\n")

if (!file.exists(weather_file_path)) {
  stop("Error: Weather data file not found at: ", weather_file_path)
}

# Import weather data with multiple encoding attempts
weather_data <- NULL

tryCatch({
  weather_data <- read_csv2(weather_file_path, 
                           locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8", decimal_mark = ","), 
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
  cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (UTF-8)\n")
}, error = function(e) {
  tryCatch({
    weather_data <<- read_csv2(weather_file_path, 
                              locale = locale(encoding = "latin1", decimal_mark = ","), 
                              show_col_types = FALSE)
    cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (latin1)\n")
  }, error = function(e2) {
    tryCatch({
      weather_data <<- read_csv2(weather_file_path, 
                                locale = locale(encoding = "CP1252", decimal_mark = ","), 
                                show_col_types = FALSE)
      cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (CP1252)\n")
    }, error = function(e3) {
      weather_data <<- read.csv(weather_file_path, sep = ";", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, 
                               encoding = "UTF-8", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
      cat("  ✓ Weather data imported (base R)\n")
    })
  })
})

# Clean column names
if (!is.null(weather_data)) {
  original_names <- names(weather_data)
  clean_names <- iconv(original_names, from = "UTF-8", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
  clean_names <- gsub("T�\\(C\\)", "T_C", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("Cl�", "Cle", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("P�riode", "Periode", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("D�cade", "Decade", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("Ann�e", "Annee", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("S�n�gal", "Senegal", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("�", "e", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("�", "a", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._]", "_", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("__+", "_", clean_names)
  clean_names <- gsub("^_|_$", "", clean_names)
  names(weather_data) <- clean_names
  cat("  ✓ Column names cleaned\n")
}

cat("  Weather data:", nrow(weather_data), "records\n")
cat("  Date range:", as.character(range(weather_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: PARSE DATES IN PARCELS

cat("Step 3: Parsing dates in parcels...\n")

# Function to parse dates flexibly
parse_flexible_date <- function(date_string) {
  if (inherits(date_string, "Date")) return(date_string)
  date_string <- as.character(date_string)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(dmy(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(mdy(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(ymd(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%d/%m/%Y"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string, format = "%Y-%m-%d"))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_string))
  if (!is.na(result)) return(result)
  
  return(as.Date(NA))
}

# Parse planting and harvest dates
parcels <- parcels %>%
  mutate(
    planting_date = sapply(SC_planting_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% 
      as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01"),
    harvest_date = sapply(SC_harvest_date, parse_flexible_date) %>% 
      as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01")
  )

# Check validity
weather_date_range <- range(weather_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE)
valid_records <- !is.na(parcels$planting_date) & 
                 !is.na(parcels$harvest_date) & 
                 parcels$planting_date < parcels$harvest_date &
                 parcels$planting_date >= weather_date_range[1] & 
                 parcels$harvest_date <= weather_date_range[2]

cat("  Valid growing periods:", sum(valid_records), "out of", nrow(parcels), "\n")
cat("  Date range:", as.character(range(parcels$planting_date[valid_records], na.rm = TRUE)), "to",
    as.character(range(parcels$harvest_date[valid_records], na.rm = TRUE)), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: HELPER FUNCTIONS FOR EXTREME INDICES
# ============================================================================

# Function to calculate consecutive days
calc_consecutive_days <- function(condition_vector) {
  if (length(condition_vector) == 0 || all(is.na(condition_vector))) return(0)
  
  # Replace NA with FALSE for consecutive calculation
  condition_clean <- ifelse(is.na(condition_vector), FALSE, condition_vector)
  
  if (!any(condition_clean)) return(0)
  
  # Calculate runs of TRUE values
  rle_result <- rle(condition_clean)
  max_consecutive <- max(rle_result$lengths[rle_result$values], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  return(ifelse(is.finite(max_consecutive), max_consecutive, 0))
}

# Function to calculate rolling maximum for n-day rainfall
calc_rolling_max <- function(values, n) {
  if (length(values) < n || all(is.na(values))) return(NA)
  
  # Replace NA with 0 for precipitation calculations
  values_clean <- ifelse(is.na(values), 0, values)
  
  if (length(values_clean) < n) return(sum(values_clean, na.rm = TRUE))
  
  # Calculate rolling sums and find maximum
  rolling_sums <- zoo::rollsum(values_clean, k = n, align = "left", fill = NA)
  return(max(rolling_sums, na.rm = TRUE))
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: ENHANCED WEATHER CALCULATION FUNCTION WITH EXTREME INDICES
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 4: Setting up enhanced weather calculation function...\n")

# Enhanced function to calculate all weather statistics including extreme indices
calculate_enhanced_weather_stats <- function(plant_date, harvest_date, weather_df) {
  if (is.na(plant_date) || is.na(harvest_date) || plant_date >= harvest_date) {
    return(list(
      # Basic temperature means
      temp_mini_mean = NA, temp_maxi_mean = NA, temp_moy_mean = NA, ampl_mean = NA,
      # Humidity means  
      h_mini_mean = NA, h_maxi_mean = NA, h_moy_mean = NA,
      h_6h_mean = NA, h_12h_mean = NA, h_16h_mean = NA, h_24h_mean = NA,
      # Simplified soil temperature means
      soil_temp_6h_mean = NA, soil_temp_16h_mean = NA,
      # Basic accumulations
      precipitation_weather_total = NA, radiation_total = NA, 
      radiation_ERA_total = NA, evaporation_total = NA,
      growing_period_days_weather = NA,
      
      # EXTREME RAINFALL INDICES (ERI)
      CWD = NA,  # Consecutive wet days
      CDD = NA,  # Consecutive dry days  
      SDII = NA, # Simple daily rainfall intensity
      R10 = NA,  # Heavy rainfall days (≥10mm)
      R20 = NA,  # Very heavy rainfall days (≥20mm)
      Rx1 = NA,  # Max 1-day rainfall
      Rx5 = NA,  # Max 5-day rainfall
      R95p = NA, # Extremely wet days (>95th percentile)
      R99p = NA, # Extremely wet days (>99th percentile)
      
      # EXTREME TEMPERATURE INDICES (ETI)
      HD = NA,   # Hot days (>35°C)
      TNn = NA,  # Minimum daily minimum temperature
      TNx = NA,  # Maximum daily minimum temperature
      TXn = NA,  # Minimum daily maximum temperature
      TXx = NA   # Maximum daily maximum temperature
    ))
  }
  
  # Filter weather data for the growing period
  period_weather <- weather_df[weather_df$Date >= plant_date & weather_df$Date <= harvest_date, ]
  
  if (nrow(period_weather) == 0) {
    return(list(
      temp_mini_mean = NA, temp_maxi_mean = NA, temp_moy_mean = NA, ampl_mean = NA,
      h_mini_mean = NA, h_maxi_mean = NA, h_moy_mean = NA,
      h_6h_mean = NA, h_12h_mean = NA, h_16h_mean = NA, h_24h_mean = NA,
      soil_temp_6h_mean = NA, soil_temp_16h_mean = NA,
      precipitation_weather_total = NA, radiation_total = NA, 
      radiation_ERA_total = NA, evaporation_total = NA,
      growing_period_days_weather = as.numeric(harvest_date - plant_date),
      CWD = NA, CDD = NA, SDII = NA, R10 = NA, R20 = NA, Rx1 = NA, Rx5 = NA, R95p = NA, R99p = NA,
      HD = NA, TNn = NA, TNx = NA, TXn = NA, TXx = NA
    ))
  }
  
  # Basic calculations
  precip <- period_weather$precipitation_stations_mean
  temp_min <- period_weather$T_C_mini
  temp_max <- period_weather$T_C_maxi
  
  # Replace NA precipitation with 0 for most calculations
  precip_clean <- ifelse(is.na(precip), 0, precip)
  
  # Calculate simplified soil temperature means
  # Average all soil depths at 6h
  soil_6h_temps <- cbind(
    period_weather$T_6h_10_cm_Ir,
    period_weather$T_6h_20_cm_Ir,
    period_weather$T_6h_30_cm_Ir,
    period_weather$T_6h_50_cm_Ir
  )
  soil_temp_6h_mean <- mean(soil_6h_temps, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Average all soil depths at 16h
  soil_16h_temps <- cbind(
    period_weather$T_16h_10_cm_Ir,
    period_weather$T_16h_20_cm_Ir,
    period_weather$T_16h_30_cm_Ir,
    period_weather$T_16h_50_cm_Ir
  )
  soil_temp_16h_mean <- mean(soil_16h_temps, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # ===== BASIC STATISTICS =====
  basic_stats <- list(
    # Temperature means
    temp_mini_mean = mean(temp_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    temp_maxi_mean = mean(temp_max, na.rm = TRUE),
    temp_moy_mean = mean(period_weather$T_C_moy, na.rm = TRUE),
    ampl_mean = mean(period_weather$Ampl, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Humidity means
    h_mini_mean = mean(period_weather$H_Mini, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_maxi_mean = mean(period_weather$H_Maxi, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_moy_mean = mean(period_weather$H_Moy, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_6h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_6_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_12h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_12_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_16h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_16_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    h_24h_mean = mean(period_weather$H_24_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Simplified soil temperature means
    soil_temp_6h_mean = soil_temp_6h_mean,
    soil_temp_16h_mean = soil_temp_16h_mean,
    
    # Basic accumulations (renamed to avoid conflicts)
    precipitation_weather_total = sum(precip_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    radiation_total = sum(period_weather$Radiation, na.rm = TRUE),
    radiation_ERA_total = sum(period_weather$Radiation_ERA, na.rm = TRUE),
    evaporation_total = sum(period_weather$Ev_C2, na.rm = TRUE),
    growing_period_days_weather = as.numeric(harvest_date - plant_date)
  )
  
  # ===== EXTREME RAINFALL INDICES (ERI) =====
  
  # CWD: Consecutive wet days (≥1mm)
  wet_days <- precip_clean >= 1
  CWD <- calc_consecutive_days(wet_days)
  
  # CDD: Consecutive dry days (<1mm)
  dry_days <- precip_clean < 1
  CDD <- calc_consecutive_days(dry_days)
  
  # SDII: Simple daily rainfall intensity (total rainfall / wet days)
  wet_day_count <- sum(precip_clean >= 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_precip <- sum(precip_clean, na.rm = TRUE)
  SDII <- ifelse(wet_day_count > 0, total_precip / wet_day_count, NA)
  
  # R10: Heavy rainfall days (≥10mm)
  R10 <- sum(precip_clean >= 10, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # R20: Very heavy rainfall days (≥20mm)
  R20 <- sum(precip_clean >= 20, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Rx1: Max 1-day rainfall
  Rx1 <- max(precip_clean, na.rm = TRUE)
  Rx1 <- ifelse(is.finite(Rx1), Rx1, NA)
  
  # Rx5: Max 5-day rainfall
  Rx5 <- calc_rolling_max(precip_clean, 5)
  
  # Calculate percentiles for the growing season (only for days with precipitation > 0)
  wet_precip <- precip_clean[precip_clean > 0]
  if (length(wet_precip) >= 5) {  # Need at least 5 wet days for meaningful percentiles
    p95 <- quantile(wet_precip, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
    p99 <- quantile(wet_precip, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # R95p: Total rainfall on extremely wet days (>95th percentile)
    R95p <- sum(precip_clean[precip_clean > p95], na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # R99p: Total rainfall on extremely wet days (>99th percentile)  
    R99p <- sum(precip_clean[precip_clean > p99], na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    R95p <- NA
    R99p <- NA
  }
  
  # ===== EXTREME TEMPERATURE INDICES (ETI) =====
  
  # HD: Hot days (maximum temperature > 35°C)
  HD <- sum(temp_max > 35, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Temperature extremes
  TNn <- min(temp_min, na.rm = TRUE)  # Minimum daily minimum temperature
  TNx <- max(temp_min, na.rm = TRUE)  # Maximum daily minimum temperature
  TXn <- min(temp_max, na.rm = TRUE)  # Minimum daily maximum temperature
  TXx <- max(temp_max, na.rm = TRUE)  # Maximum daily maximum temperature
  
  # Handle infinite values
  TNn <- ifelse(is.finite(TNn), TNn, NA)
  TNx <- ifelse(is.finite(TNx), TNx, NA)
  TXn <- ifelse(is.finite(TXn), TXn, NA)
  TXx <- ifelse(is.finite(TXx), TXx, NA)
  
  # Combine all statistics
  extreme_stats <- list(
    CWD = CWD, CDD = CDD, SDII = SDII, R10 = R10, R20 = R20,
    Rx1 = Rx1, Rx5 = Rx5, R95p = R95p, R99p = R99p,
    HD = HD, TNn = TNn, TNx = TNx, TXn = TXn, TXx = TXx
  )
  
  # Convert NaN to NA for cleaner output
  all_stats <- c(basic_stats, extreme_stats)
  all_stats <- lapply(all_stats, function(x) if(is.nan(x)) NA else x)
  
  return(all_stats)
}

cat("  ✓ Enhanced calculation function ready\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: CALCULATE ENHANCED WEATHER STATISTICS FOR EACH PARCEL
# ============================================================================

cat("Step 5: Calculating enhanced weather statistics with extreme indices...\n")

# Initialize enhanced weather variables dataframe
n_total <- nrow(parcels)
enhanced_weather_vars <- data.frame(
  # Basic variables
  temp_mini_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  temp_maxi_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  temp_moy_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  ampl_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_mini_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_maxi_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_moy_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_6h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_12h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_16h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  h_24h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  # Simplified soil temperature variables
  soil_temp_6h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  soil_temp_16h_mean = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  precipitation_weather_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  radiation_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  radiation_ERA_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  evaporation_total = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  growing_period_days_weather = rep(NA_real_, n_total),
  
  # Extreme Rainfall Indices (ERI)
  CWD = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Consecutive wet days
  CDD = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Consecutive dry days
  SDII = rep(NA_real_, n_total),  # Simple daily intensity index
  R10 = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Heavy rainfall days
  R20 = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Very heavy rainfall days
  Rx1 = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Max 1-day rainfall
  Rx5 = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Max 5-day rainfall
  R95p = rep(NA_real_, n_total),  # Extremely wet days (95th percentile)
  R99p = rep(NA_real_, n_total),  # Extremely wet days (99th percentile)
  
  # Extreme Temperature Indices (ETI)
  HD = rep(NA_real_, n_total),    # Hot days
  TNn = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Minimum daily minimum temperature
  TNx = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Maximum daily minimum temperature
  TXn = rep(NA_real_, n_total),   # Minimum daily maximum temperature
  TXx = rep(NA_real_, n_total)    # Maximum daily maximum temperature
)

# Process each parcel with progress tracking
chunk_size <- ceiling(n_total / 10)
start_time <- Sys.time()

for (i in 1:n_total) {
  if (i %% chunk_size == 0 || i == n_total) {
    elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))
    remaining <- (elapsed / i) * (n_total - i)
    cat("  Processing:", i, "/", n_total, "(", round(100*i/n_total, 1), "%) - ",
        "Elapsed:", round(elapsed, 1), "min, Est. remaining:", round(remaining, 1), "min\n")
  }
  
  stats <- calculate_enhanced_weather_stats(
    plant_date = parcels$planting_date[i],
    harvest_date = parcels$harvest_date[i],
    weather_df = weather_data
  )
  
  # Assign results
  for (var_name in names(stats)) {
    if (var_name %in% names(enhanced_weather_vars)) {
      enhanced_weather_vars[i, var_name] <- stats[[var_name]]
    }
  }
}

total_time <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))
cat("  Total processing time:", round(total_time, 1), "minutes\n")
cat("  Completed!\n\n")

cat("Step 6: Merging enhanced weather data with parcels...\n")

# Combine parcels with enhanced weather variables
parcels_with_enhanced_weather <- cbind(
  parcels %>% select(-planting_date, -harvest_date),  # Remove temp date columns
  enhanced_weather_vars
)

# Count successful calculations
n_with_weather <- sum(!is.na(enhanced_weather_vars$growing_period_days_weather))

cat("  Records with weather data:", n_with_weather, "\n")
cat("  Records without weather data:", n_total - n_with_weather, "\n")

if (nrow(valid_weather) > 0) {

  for (var in eri_vars) {

      sprintf("%.0f", max(valid_weather$growing_period_days_weather, na.rm = TRUE)), "days\n\n")
}
```

# IV. Complete Data Extraction to CSV

After constructing our comprehensive spatially-enabled geopackage with all soil properties, sugarcane agronomics, rainfall, basic weather statistics, and extreme indices, we need a format suitable for statistical analysis and machine learning. This final section extracts the complete dataset into a tabular CSV format, removing the spatial geometry while retaining all analytical variables. The script carefully selects and orders variables into logical groups: target variables like yield and sugar content, soil chemical and physical properties, management practices, basic weather summaries, and all extreme weather indices. It also performs final data quality corrections, particularly fixing known issues with harvest method coding in specific years using intelligent interpolation from adjacent years. The result is a clean, analysis-ready CSV file containing over fifty variables across thousands of parcel-year observations, with clear variable names and comprehensive documentation of what each column represents. This dataset serves as the direct input for exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, and machine learning pipelines aimed at understanding and predicting sugarcane yield and quality.

```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# ============================================================================
# EXTRACT SUBSET AND EXPORT TO CSV (WITH ADDITIONAL VARIABLES)
# ============================================================================

# Load the geopackage
input_gpkg <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/parcels_MERGED_soil_sugarcane_with_weather_extreme_indices.gpkg"
output_csv <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/final_dataset_for_analysis_with_quality_metrics.csv"

cat("Loading geopackage...\n")
parcels <- st_read(input_gpkg, quiet = TRUE)

# Function to extract campaign year from campaign variable
extract_campaign_year <- function(campaign_string) {
  if (is.na(campaign_string) || campaign_string == "") {
    return(NA)
  }
  
  campaign_clean <- trimws(as.character(campaign_string))
  
  if (grepl("-", campaign_clean)) {
    year_part <- strsplit(campaign_clean, "-")[[1]][1]
    
    if (nchar(year_part) == 2) {
      year_num <- as.numeric(year_part)
      
      if (year_num <= 30) {
        campaign_year <- 2000 + year_num
      } else {
        campaign_year <- 1900 + year_num
      }
    } else if (nchar(year_part) == 4) {
      campaign_year <- as.numeric(year_part)
    } else {
      return(NA)
    }
    
    return(campaign_year)
  }
  
  return(NA)
}

# Create campaign_year variable
cat("Extracting campaign year...\n")
parcels$campaign_year <- sapply(parcels$SC_Campaign, extract_campaign_year)

cat("Valid campaign years:", sum(!is.na(parcels$campaign_year)), "out of", nrow(parcels), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# FIX SC_HARVEST ISSUES
# ============================================================================

cat("Fixing SC_harvest issues...\n")

# First, standardize the encoding issue with "Mécanique"
parcels$SC_harvest <- as.character(parcels$SC_harvest)
parcels$SC_harvest[!is.na(parcels$SC_harvest) & grepl("M.*canique", parcels$SC_harvest, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- "Mécanique"

# Create a lookup table for each parcel's harvest type by year
harvest_lookup <- parcels %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(field, campaign_year, SC_harvest) %>%
  filter(!is.na(campaign_year))

# Function to get harvest value from adjacent years
get_adjacent_harvest <- function(field_id, target_year, lookup_data) {
  parcel_data <- lookup_data %>% filter(field == !!field_id)
  
  # Get values from adjacent years
  prev_year <- parcel_data %>% filter(campaign_year == target_year - 1) %>% pull(SC_harvest)
  next_year <- parcel_data %>% filter(campaign_year == target_year + 1) %>% pull(SC_harvest)
  
  # Remove NA values
  adjacent_values <- c(prev_year, next_year)
  adjacent_values <- adjacent_values[!is.na(adjacent_values)]
  
  if (length(adjacent_values) == 0) {
    return(NA)
  } else if (length(adjacent_values) == 1) {
    return(adjacent_values[1])
  } else {
    # If both years available and they match, use that value
    if (adjacent_values[1] == adjacent_values[2]) {
      return(adjacent_values[1])
    } else {
      # If they differ, use the most recent one (next year)
      return(adjacent_values[length(adjacent_values)])
    }
  }
}

# Fix 2010 (all NA)
cat("Fixing 2010 SC_harvest values...\n")
rows_2010 <- which(parcels$campaign_year == 2010)
cat("Found", length(rows_2010), "rows for year 2010\n")

for (i in rows_2010) {
  new_value <- get_adjacent_harvest(parcels$field[i], 2010, harvest_lookup)
  parcels$SC_harvest[i] <- new_value
}

# Fix 2021 (all incorrectly set to "Manuelle")
cat("Fixing 2021 SC_harvest values...\n")
rows_2021 <- which(parcels$campaign_year == 2021)
cat("Found", length(rows_2021), "rows for year 2021\n")

for (i in rows_2021) {
  new_value <- get_adjacent_harvest(parcels$field[i], 2021, harvest_lookup)
  parcels$SC_harvest[i] <- new_value
}

cat("SC_harvest correction complete!\n")
cat("Current SC_harvest distribution:\n")
print(table(parcels$SC_harvest, parcels$campaign_year, useNA = "ifany"))
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# DEFINE VARIABLES TO KEEP (WITH ADDITIONAL QUALITY METRICS)
# ============================================================================

# Define variables to keep (in order)
variables_to_keep <- c(
  # Target and key variables
  "SC_tc_per_ha_actual",
  "SC_brix_percent",
  "SC_variety",
  "SC_irrigation_type",
  "SC_crop_cycle",
  "SC_harvest",
  "campaign_year",
  "pH_complete",
  
  # Soil chemical properties
  "Exchangeable_Calcium_meq_100g_complete",

  "Clay_percent_complete",

  # Soil organic matter

  "temp_mini_mean",

  # Basic weather - Humidity
  "h_mini_mean",

  "h_6h_mean",
  "h_12h_mean",
  "h_16h_mean",
  "h_24h_mean",
  
  # Basic weather - Soil temperature
  "soil_temp_6h_mean",

  # Basic weather - Radiation and evaporation
  "radiation_total",
  "radiation_ERA_total",
  "evaporation_total",
  "growing_period_days_weather",
  
  # Extreme Rainfall Indices (ERI)
  "CWD",
  "CDD",
  "SDII",
  "R10",

  "Rx1",
  "Rx5",

  # Extreme Temperature Indices (ETI)
  "HD",
  "TNn",

  "TXx",
  
  # ========================================
  # NEW: Sugarcane Quality Metrics
  # ========================================
  "SC_tc_per_ha_per_week",
  "SC_tc_per_ha_52_weeks",
  "SC_pol_juice_percent",
  "SC_purity_percent",
  "SC_fiber_percent",
  "SC_pol_cane_percent",
  "SC_glucose_cane_percent",
  "SC_hugot_sugar"
)

# Check which variables exist
existing_vars <- variables_to_keep[variables_to_keep %in% names(parcels)]
missing_vars <- variables_to_keep[!variables_to_keep %in% names(parcels)]

if (length(missing_vars) > 0) {
  cat("WARNING: Missing variables:\n")
  print(missing_vars)
  cat("\n")
}

cat("Total variables requested:", length(variables_to_keep), "\n")
cat("Variables found:", length(existing_vars), "\n")
cat("Variables missing:", length(missing_vars), "\n\n")

# Create subset (remove geometry for CSV)
cat("Creating subset with", length(existing_vars), "variables...\n")
subset_data <- parcels %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(all_of(existing_vars))

# Export to CSV
cat("Exporting to CSV...\n")
write.csv(subset_data, output_csv, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== EXPORT COMPLETE ===\n")
cat("Output file:", output_csv, "\n")
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(subset_data), "\n")
cat("Number of columns:", ncol(subset_data), "\n")
cat("File size:", round(file.size(output_csv) / 1024^2, 2), "MB\n\n")

# Display first few rows
cat("First 5 rows preview:\n")
print(head(subset_data, 5))

# Display SC_harvest summary
cat("\n=== SC_HARVEST SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Distribution by harvest type:\n")
print(table(subset_data$SC_harvest, useNA = "ifany"))
cat("\nDistribution by year:\n")
print(table(subset_data$campaign_year, subset_data$SC_harvest, useNA = "ifany"))

# Display summary statistics for new quality metrics
cat("\n=== NEW QUALITY METRICS SUMMARY ===\n")
quality_vars <- c("SC_pol_juice_percent", "SC_purity_percent", "SC_fiber_percent", 
                  "SC_pol_cane_percent", "SC_hugot_sugar", "SC_tsr")
quality_vars_present <- quality_vars[quality_vars %in% names(subset_data)]

if (length(quality_vars_present) > 0) {
  for (var in quality_vars_present) {
    cat("\n", var, ":\n", sep = "")
    print(summary(subset_data[[var]]))
  }
} else {
  cat("None of the quality metric variables were found in the dataset.\n")
}
```
